title: PHP security releases fix critical bugs (19 Nov)
summary: The PHP project shipped security releases for every supported branch on 19 November 2026: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 (PHP 8.6.0 also reached GA the same day). The pre-announcement rated the highest severity CRITICAL and said the critical issues need a non-default configuration or an uncommon setup. The 8.5.13 changelog lists, among others, use-after-free bugs in magic-method backtraces (CVE-2026-129474) and the timezone cache (CVE-2026-129496) that can lead to remote code execution, a PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction (CVE-2026-129538), a double free during DOM XML serialization (CVE-2026-129501) and a use-after-free after shutdown (CVE-2026-129182). This follows the PHP2Shell releases earlier this autumn.
why: PHP runs under a lot of admin tooling: WordPress and intranet sites, helpdesk and monitoring portals, and appliances that bundle it. The CGI bug matters most where PHP is still run as CGI rather than PHP-FPM or a module.
todo: Do now: inventory PHP versions on servers and containers and upgrade to 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (or your distribution's backport).
Prioritise internet-facing hosts and any that run PHP as CGI; rebuild container images rather than patching running ones.
Wait for vendor updates for appliances and products that bundle PHP, and track their advisories. CVSS scores were not published on php.net at the time of writing.
